messages:
oliver: Canary p95 decode increased ~18% after today's deploy at 11:20 UTC. Not seeing throughput loss, just tail decode latency.

maya: ugh, can you paste the p50/p95/p99 numbers and model?

oliver: model=redwood/llama-rlhf-7b; p50 42ms->45ms, p95 320ms->380ms, p99 560ms->820ms. No GPU saturation spikes.

ton y: devops-bot already paused the canary at 20% (rollout policy). Holding until triage. :rotating_light:

jen: devops-bot: canary hold recorded for runtime/ab12c3f (auto policy: p95 delta > 15%).

devops-bot: Canary rollout paused by policy. Trigger: latency-regression. Commit: ab12c3f.

maya: timeline: ab12c3f rolled at 11:18am. PR #4823 merged earlier today — batching heuristic change + fused-embed op landing. I'm going to bisect quickly.

tony: I started a local bisect against the canary repro. Quick summary of commands I ran:
```
git bisect start HEAD ab12c3f^
# run perf harness: tests/perf/replicate_canary.sh --model llama-rlhf-7b
# measure p95 from harness
```
Found culprit: commit b3f9a113 (PR 4823: adaptive-batch-delay + fused-embed micro-opt).

oliver: interesting. b3f9a113 toggles new batch gating: it reduces max_batch_wait_ms to 4ms for small requests which increases small-batch frequency. Also in same PR the fused-embed op changed scratch allocation to reuse KV buffers.

sophia: Could increased small batches cause more KV cache thrash / evictions? That would explain decode tail jumps without GPU saturation.

ton y: profile snapshot (shortened) shows frequent kernel switch and extra memcpy in decode path: 
```
# perf timeline (simplified)
decode_step: attn_fused_v2 (fast) -> memcpy -> attn_scalar (slow fallback) -> memcpy back
memcpy count: +220% relative to baseline
KV cache: lookups increased, eviction count +45%
```

oliver: nvprof sample showed these kernels alternating and stalls on CUDA memcpy. Also saw small GPU kernels run more often which hurts tail because of kernel-launch overhead.

maya: so two hypothesis: (1) new batch heuristic causing many tiny batches (kernel launch overhead), (2) fused-embed reuse of buffer collides with KV cache eviction policy causing more cache misses + memcpy.

jen: do we have a quick flag we can flip to roll back only the heuristic? We want minimal impact for Hosted customers.

ton y: yes — runtime has feature flags. You can force legacy batching via env `RUNTIME_DISABLE_ADAPTIVE_BATCH_DELAY=1` or force old fused-embed via `RUNTIME_LEGACY_EMBED_OP=1`.

sophia: let's flip batching first (less invasive) and re-run the canary harness. If that fixes p95, we can promote a targeted rollback.

oliver: I applied `RUNTIME_DISABLE_ADAPTIVE_BATCH_DELAY=1` to the canary instances and restarted the worker. Re-running harness now.

(30s later)

maya: early numbers after toggling batching: p95 down from 380ms -> 330ms, p99 820ms -> 640ms. Improvement but still not baseline.

tony: partial improvement suggests batching was a big contributor but fused-embed behavior still causing residual tail. I reproduced the KV eviction pattern locally by running high-concurrency prefix traffic. Evictions spike when fused-embed reuses scratch memory on sequential decode boundaries.

oliver: snippet from local perf log: 
```
KV_evictions: 124 -> 180 (with fused-embed reuse)
KV_miss_latency: +12ms p95
kernel_launchs/sec: +28%
```

jen: this is a rollout blocker for the full release. Ops: keep canary paused. Engineering: prioritize a revert of the fused-embed change and keep batching flag off in prod for now.

maya: proposed action items:
- revert commit b3f9a113 (fused-embed + adaptive-batch) in a targeted patch OR revert fused-embed only (smaller PR) 
- keep `RUNTIME_DISABLE_ADAPTIVE_BATCH_DELAY=1` in canary and staged but allow safe rollout for other models
- add unit/integration perf test in CI that simulates KV-heavy long-context patterns

tony: I'll open the revert PR now (small revert for fused-embed portion). If CI perf test fails, we block merge.

jen: ops will keep the canary hold. I'll coordinate customer comms if this expands.

devops-bot: Canary rollback flag set by jen. Notifying stakeholders channel #incidents.

oliver: one last thought — let's add a perf metric that tracks `memcpy_count` and `kernel-switch-rate` per request so future regressions hit an alert sooner.

sophia: agreed. I'll add that metric to runtime telemetry and a simple smoke test in the perf harness.

maya: thanks all. Revert PR expected in ~20m. We'll re-run full canary after merge and then decide on rollback vs patch. :thumbsup:
